items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Most names follow FFmpeg's (lumXInc, chrSrcHSub, fullChr) and there are useful header comments. But single-letter names run through the logic: `c: *m.Ctx`, `s: m.Planes`, `d`, `f`, module aliases `m`/`k`, plus `fs`, `dd`, `ddd`, `f2s`, `ii`. That caps this at accept.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: filter.init ports initFilter in one function: coefficient generation, the reduce/cutoff loops and border fixing. It is clearly over 100 lines, which caps this at bad. kernels.zig is very large (~100k chars of edits). Main is split into create/initGeneric/generic.run, and helper scripts were removed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: swscale_create checks the format range and positive sizes, and allocation failures return null via `catch return null`. Some constants are bare (`+ 64` padding, `31` alignment, 10066329 is commented). Known gap: extreme downscales with 256+ taps give 33–39 dB, below the 40 dB bar.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: Rows are read through strides (`s.row(plane, r)`). The agent tested 376 extra configs, including 1x1, 3x5 and 641x479, for all format pairs. But very large downscale ratios (e.g. 1280x720 to 3x2) fall below the accuracy bar because the cascaded context is missing, and unsupported configs only get basic null checks.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: build.zig pins `cpu_model = .explicit = &x86_64_v3`. `nm -D` shows only swscale_create/process/destroy exported, objdump finds no zmm/k-register use, filters are precomputed in swscale_create, there are no threads, and the fast_gather tweak was removed.
